title: Paris audience boos sophisticated numbers
summary: In Paris the audience resented a girl singer humming sophisticated pieces and wanted jazz.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But regardless of what the critics said, the audiences obviously were quite happy with the music they were hearing. Isn't that right?

Most of them. The only time I ever heard the audience resent what was going on was in France, in Paris one time. They -- Ellington had gotten to the place where he was playing these very sophisticated things, and well, the audience just resented it completely and starting booing. And especially when the little singer was singing these humming type of things. They wanted to hear they booed, stoms -- and jazz -- they didn't want to hear that pretty stuff.
Was that Ozzie Bailey?
No, that was a little girl. Yeah, they didn't want to hear that.
What year was that, which trip (inaudible)?
Oh no, I can't -- it was one of the European -- you know, we went to Europe so many times.
Yeah, because I remember Duke told me
once when you went there that -- I think it was the San-Play-elle --
Salle Pleyel
Yeah. That's where it was.
-- that Ossie Bailey was singing "Autumn Leaves" in French, and Duke thought -- he said I thought this would really please the French people to have --
Ozzie
No.
-- to hear us performing in the French language. And he said they booed Ossie right off the stage when he started singing French.
Ozzie
Well, that must be another time --
Oh -- well, I heard --
-- because this is the time that this little girl was humming, you know that -- I mean no words --
Right.
-- and the stuff was far too sophisticated for the audience. They wanted to hear some jazz. They didn't want to hear that stuff.
You don't remember which girl singer this was,

No, I doesn't. So, that was one time. You see people -- you can't force your ego on people, you see. They pay for that performance and they want to hear what they want to hear, and that's the way they are in Europe. They don't want to hear what you want to make them hear. They want to hear what they want to hear. And I guess still today they
do the same thing if they didn't like what was going on. So, that's only natural.
